characters.description: The Malefic Viper's Chosen begins his final challenge as a neutral Guild courier. With his level concealed, he relies on stealth, alchemy, mobility, and resistance to karmic scrutiny while navigating jobs whose apparent instructions cannot always be trusted.
characters.name: Jake Thayne

characters.description: A powerful B-grade in a mid-sized city and the intended recipient of a living fire elemental. Jake must carry the unstable captive to him covertly and without teleportation before its failing containment breaks.
characters.name: Infernal Baron

characters.description: A hooded envoy for a powerful organization seeking the fire elemental. The envoy remotely kills the failed interception group with karmic magic and offers Jake a competing delivery arrangement.
characters.name: Hooded representative

characters.description: An A-grade noble, father of the Infernal Baron, and the true client behind Jake's elemental delivery. His family consumes elementals to strengthen its flame path, and he recruits Jake to infiltrate the organization attacking his lineage.
characters.name: Duke of Flames

characters.description: A major creator of the newly built courier challenge dungeon. The simplified setting bears signs of exploitable design choices, making his work an important part of the divine observation surrounding Jake's run.
characters.name: Minaga

characters.description: A B-grade Marquise and senior member of the elemental-rights organization. Jake learns that she is the hooded representative who approached him during the elemental delivery.
characters.name: B-grade Marquise

characters.description: The Duke of Flames’ daughter rejects her family’s practice of consuming elementals. After initially cooperating with the elemental-rights organization, she works through another dukedom to turn it and her father’s faction against each other.
characters.name: Duke of Flames’ daughter

characters.description: The disguised founder of the neutral courier Guild and an S-grade veteran of the old dragon war. After testing Jake's loyalties, he finds that noble coercion has compromised his institution and asks Jake to help expose the abuse.
characters.name: Guild founder

characters.description: Jake's primordial patron. The records behind his power allow Jake's Shroud of the Primordial to resist even very high-grade karmic detection, protecting Jake's claimed neutrality during the courier challenge.
characters.name: Malefic Viper

characters.description: An exiled S-grade dragonkin whose aid may decide the renewed war against the Dragon Tribe. Jake's final courier assignment is to locate him through a legendary horn and persuade him to enter a conflict for which he has no natural loyalty.
characters.name: Forsaken Dragonkin

characters.description: Jake's wind-aligned companion and fellow challenger. Her courier run is chaotic and earns her a rare medallion.
characters.name: Sylphie

characters.description: Jake's swordsman companion and an affiliate of Aeon Clock. In his courier challenge he brokers a temporary peace among the major powers, earning a legendary medallion while paying for the result with two lives.
characters.name: Sword Saint

characters.description: The party's plant and life-magic specialist. She resolves her courier world's crisis by using her bloodline and a living planet to relocate its enlightened peoples instead of winning the central war directly.
characters.name: Dina

characters.description: The party's soul-magic specialist. His system-recognized kingship and ability to detect deception are strong assets in the courier challenge, although his limited delivery speed leaves him still working when Jake finishes.
characters.name: Fallen King

characters.description: A war god associated with Valhall. Jake defeats Valdemar's challenge image and later reports that the true god is far more dangerous.
characters.name: Valdemar

characters.description: The level-320 robotic controller of the Nine Towers experiment. It directs golems and the orbital network against Jake's party after they discover that the supposed terraforming system is designed to exterminate life outside its towers.
characters.name: Chief Overseer

characters.description: An old friend of Jake associated with the Risen. Divine observers describe him as a promising dungeon engineer whose progress has exceeded expectations, although they consider Jake's altered soul and bloodline a poor match for recruitment into the same faction.
characters.name: Casper

characters.description: The shared identity behind the two ogre rulers of floor 80. Jake discovers that the apparent emperors are independent halves of one twin-head being with a single true soul, making their eventual merged form the likely event boss.
characters.name: Twinhead Emperor

characters.description: A Valhall Rune Maiden and elite Nevermore challenger. She fights on floor 80 with a reshuffled Valhall-associated party after its roster changes near the end of the run, continuing the faction's attempt to secure a strong closing result.
characters.name: Carmen

characters.description: Jake's rival C-grade challenger. His party clears the same floor-80 objective by reconciling the divided emperors rather than battling their merged form, placing him among the leading contenders for the final rankings.
characters.name: Yip of Yore's Chosen

characters.description: The public host who appears when Nevermore City's leaderboard countdown ends. He is Minaga, now presenting the hidden rankings before the assembled competitors, divine observers, and faction delegations.
characters.name: All-God Legion

characters.description: The bound god and final authority behind the dungeon. Nevermore personally evaluates Jake in a time-paused space when his exceptional score requires a rare calculation beyond the ordinary completion process.
characters.name: Nevermore

characters.description: A goddess of the Pantheon of Life who takes an interest in Jake after his record-setting run. She considers inviting him to the Pantheon, knows that he may be interested in archery instruction, and watches the political attention gathering around him.
characters.name: Artemis

characters.description: Jake's brother and an Earth-connected competitor. After the challenge dungeons, Umbra places him with a stronger team that helps him secure a top-250 result and entry to the private post-ranking gathering.
characters.name: Caleb

characters.description: An Earth-connected elite competitor and researcher blessed by the All-Seeing. He joins Jake's group at the private gathering for highly ranked challengers after Nevermore's leaderboard ceremony, placing him among the successful returnees from their universe.
characters.name: Arnold

characters.description: An A-grade dragon chosen by the Worm God and host of the private gathering for highly ranked Nevermore competitors.
characters.name: Worm God’s chosen

characters.description: An heir of the Fourth Hell who carries a fragment of the Cerulean Devil's crystallized heart. He asks Jake to forge a complete Demon Lord heart through a dangerous, time-sensitive ritual and promises to meet a reasonable condition if it succeeds.
characters.name: Fourth Hell demon prince

characters.description: Dina’s grandfather, from whom she inherited her bloodline.
characters.name: Nature's Attendant

characters.description: The Fourth Hell prince after surviving his transformation into a full demon lord. Jake forces the Cerulean Devil's manifested records to submit within the prince's soul space, leaving the newly evolved demon alive and in control of the inherited power.
characters.name: Cerulean demon lord

characters.description: Jake's disciple and Duskleaf's chosen, now training as a healer who can also contribute directly in combat. Having previously depended on protected dungeon runs, she works to overcome panic before attempting Nevermore.
characters.name: Mira

characters.description: A succubus associated with Mira and Jake. She has a profession and demonic racial abilities but no class, and she lacks confidence in direct combat when Jake contacts her about an opportunity linked to the Fourth Hell.
characters.name: Erin

characters.description: The Primordial of Life and leader of the Pantheon of Life, embodied as a living divine realm rooted in a great planet. Matters connected to Jake's Nevermore achievement prompt her to meet Dina, Nature's Attendant, and Artemis. While examining Dina, she discovers that proximity to Jake has changed Dina's soul.
characters.name: Yggdrasil

characters.description: A returning Juvenile Cosmic Genesis Worm and Jake's unconventional travel companion. Sandy arrives at Jake's residence during his reunion with Mira and Erin.
characters.name: Sandy

characters.description: One of Earth's leaders who is in Nevermore while Arthur remains behind to govern.
characters.name: Miranda

characters.description: A level-271 mountain wyvern with a budding dragon's heart and the Greater Blessing of the Everfrost Dragon God. It defeats a raid by the Sword Saint's vampire clansmen but ends the battle wounded and depleted, with living captives in its cave.
characters.name: North Peak Wyvern

recaps.ending: Jake finishes Nevermore as its all-time C-grade record holder, while his five-person party survives and disperses. Sylphie, the Sword Saint, and the Fallen King head toward Earth, Dina returns to the Pantheon of Life, and Jake remains briefly in Nevermore City. Yip of Yore's faction shifts toward isolating him from the Malefic Viper through recruitment and public pressure. Jake keeps Valhall at a distance, becomes Carmen's partner, and helps the Fourth Hell prince evolve into a demon lord who owes him a major boon. Questions about Jake's origin energy, his effect on other souls, the karmic links in his boots, and the erased First Sage remain open. Back on Earth, Haven is stable but strained by integration. Jake leaves those politics to Miranda, settles the immediate dispute between the North Peak Wyvern and the Sword Saint's vampire clan, and spends time with Caleb, Adam, and his parents. With family communication established, Sandy carries Jake toward the moon before the Prima Guardian event.
recaps.in_short: Jake Thayne completes his last challenge dungeon by rising through a courier Guild, exposing noble corruption, and recruiting the Forsaken Dragonkin to end a returning dragon war. Reunited with Sylphie, the Sword Saint, Dina, and the Fallen King, he pushes through Nevermore's final floors. The party forces the two Twin Emperors to merge, and Sylphie's awakened authority kills the resulting boss without a party death. Jake then claims the all-time C-grade Nevermore record and becomes Peerless Conqueror of Nevermore. After resisting competing recruitment efforts, he turns a Fourth Hell prince's perilous ritual into a successful demon-lord evolution. He returns through the Order to Earth, where he leaves Haven's integration problems to Miranda, compels the North Peak Wyvern to release captured vampires, reconnects with Caleb and the rest of his family, and departs with Sandy for the moon as the Prima Guardian event approaches.

recaps.text: Previously: Jake Thayne entered Nevermore with Sylphie, the Sword Saint, Dina, and the Fallen King. Their long C-grade run took them through ordinary floors and four specialized challenge dungeons that tested combat, character, construction, and labyrinth navigation. Jake accumulated exceptional results while strengthening his arcane hunter path, his alchemy, and his bond with the Malefic Viper. His companions developed along separate paths, and their party became tied to several of the multiverse's greatest powers. Beyond Nevermore, Earth continued adapting to the System under Haven and other emerging factions preparing for future threats. Jake's brother Caleb remained connected to the Court of Shadows, Casper worked with the Risen, and the unresolved conflict with Yip of Yore's chosen continued to shadow Jake's growing reputation. One challenge remains before the party can reunite for Nevermore's closing floors: the Never-Ending Journey, which places each competitor alone in the role of a courier.

Jake begins the Never-Ending Journey in Nevermore City as a low-ranked Guild courier with his true strength concealed. His first jobs teach him that couriers receive unusual access and institutional protection but must follow instructions carefully. He advances from city deliveries to dangerous intercity work, earning better medallions and optional side assignments. His second special job is to transport a living fire elemental to the Infernal Baron before its unstable seal fails. Enemies intercept him through a false anti-smuggling group, but Jake kills their strongest mage and tracks the survivors. A hooded representative then executes its own agents remotely and offers Jake a competing delivery. Jake conceals his response, reaches the destination ahead of the deadline, and enters the Baron's warded castle in disguise. There he reveals himself privately while warning that another party is listening. The Baron kneels when a powerful flame projection appears: his father is the true client and believes Jake may serve a larger purpose.

The Duke of Flames explains that his family grows stronger by consuming elementals and asks Jake to infiltrate the organization attacking them. The opposing group also recruits Jake as an informant, leaving each side convinced he is working against the other. Jake uses this position to gather evidence while continuing enough courier work to reach Ancient rank. At a royal gathering, his Shroud of the Primordial defeats every attempt to trace his loyalties. The disguised Guild founder, an S-grade veteran, determines that Jake has remained genuinely neutral and reveals that nobles have coerced Guild workers and falsified jobs. Jake abandons the factional assignments and publicly lays out the schemes of the Duke's family, the elemental-rights organization, and a rival dukedom. The organization's leader attacks him and is killed by the Lord Protector. When the court tries to contain the scandal, the founder reveals his identity and forces action. The responsible ducal families and collaborators are detained. After months of Guild reviews and further work, Jake becomes a Legendary Courier, just as word arrives that the Dragon Tribe has returned.

A massive Dragon Tribe force approaches from another solar system, and the exposed Duke of Flames is revealed to have helped weaken the world's defenses. Jake recruits an isolated S-grade swordsman, but another supposed ally proves loyal to the invaders and collapses her trial around him. He escapes and receives the final courier job: locate the Forsaken Dragonkin and win his aid before the front fails. After months spent deciphering a legendary horn, Jake reaches the dragonkin's sanctuary while enemy forces track him. The exile demands Jake's suicide as his price. Jake refuses and instead releases a fragment of the Malefic Viper's records from within his soul, offering future guidance toward godhood. The Forsaken Dragonkin accepts, destroys the pursuers, and enters the war. His intervention secures victory. The Guild founder promotes Jake as the first mythical courier, completing the challenge. Jake leaves the dragonkin with his sincere view that advancement requires unwavering commitment to one's path. The other party members have taken very different routes through their own courier worlds, with only the Fallen King still finishing.

Jake's courier performance grants a major point award, a final-score multiplier, an all-stat title, and a mythical item capable of awakening the records of another item. He uses it on his alchemist's boots, creating a stronger mythical version with an unexplained message directing him toward a sage. The Malefic Viper recognizes the boots as his former property and says their original owner was the First Sage, his C-grade teacher from the first universe. Jake plans to investigate once his profession advances. He also upgrades his long-range marking skill through a storybook vision, gaining better soul-outline tracking and damage that increases over distance. When the party reunites, Sylphie reveals that she is the progenitor of the new Sylphian hawk lineage. The Sword Saint and Dina each earned a 70 percent challenge multiplier, the Fallen King earned 45 percent, and Jake reveals an extraordinary 105 percent total. Despite his individual leaderboard prospects, all five agree to resume the final floors as a party.

The reunited party enters the Nine Towers, where an apparent terraforming project is actually maintained by orbital systems that periodically scour the planet. They capture the towers, destroy the stations and command ship, kill the Chief Overseer, and activate a recovery protocol that ends the experiment. On the next floor, they defend expanding refugee settlements while Jake hunts the monster factions' leaders with a newly selected penetrating arrow skill. The Sword Saint's time-dilation chamber lets them turn limited outside time into months of training and combat. Over the following decade, the party clears through floor 79, including another event boss, while rapidly gaining levels. Divine observers debate Jake's path and recruitment prospects, with Valdemar openly interested and the Risen judged a poor fit for Jake's altered soul. Jake takes a new profession skill tied to his status as the Malefic Viper's Chosen but delays using it because he is also a Heretic Chosen. With Sylphie's removal deadline approaching, the party has time for only one final floor and commits to seeking its event boss.

Floor 80 contains two empires locked in a magically intensified war that has killed billions. Jake's party discovers that the rulers are independent halves of one Twinhead Ogre, using battlefields and soul-sealing bone spheres to cultivate death and curse energy. Rather than kill a separated half, the party clears the battlefields, modifies the ritual site, and uses Jake's false Lord of Hunger identity to frighten both rulers into merging. The level-335 Twinhead Emperor nearly overwhelms them. Jake's prepared arrow destroys much of one head, the party's trap drains the ritual, and the Fallen King loses an arm and leg while the others suffer severe injuries and exhaustion. The boss sacrifices one head to empower the other and traps Sylphie in hostile wind. Under the killing pressure, she upgrades her wind skill into Sylphian Authority, takes command of the surrounding wind, and kills the emperor. All five survive. They receive the floor reward, a no-death bonus, and a grand achievement for forcing the full merger. With combat finished, they prepare staggered exits designed to maximize their positions on the leaderboards.

The party reaches the final city floor and uses compounded time chambers to let each member's Nevermore timer expire in a planned order. Yip of Yore's chosen briefly leads both the current universe and era standings, while Minaga delays Jake's completion for the public ceremony. Nevermore personally calculates Jake's result: 6,075,583 points, exceeding both his rival and the previous all-time C-grade record. Jake receives the title Peerless Conqueror of Nevermore and drinks a unique restoration reward before appearing at the ceremony. His result displaces the rival and sharply raises the prestige of the Malefic Viper's faction. It also increases recruitment pressure from other powers. After the ceremony, Jake attends a private gathering for competitors who reached a top-250 position. He forms an Earth-connected group with his companions, Carmen, Caleb, Arnold, Casper, and others. An A-grade dragon chosen by the Worm God hosts the event, and a highly ranked demon prince approaches as the gathering begins.

The Fourth Hell demon prince asks Jake to forge a complete Demon Lord heart from ten legendary hearts and an inherited fragment, offering a major reward despite the risk. Casper separately asks Jake to arrange Earth passage for risen participants in the coming Prima Guardian event. A disguised primordial examines Jake's mythical boots and discovers karmic links connecting them to all twelve primordials, but cannot explain why. Carmen warns Jake that Valhall and Yip of Yore's faction are trying to separate him from the Malefic Viper. Jake's rival publicly apologizes and recasts their conflict as opposition to Jake's patron, while privately favoring recruitment over an expensive assassination. The Nevermore party disperses: Dina returns to the Pantheon of Life, Sylphie leaves for Earth with the Sword Saint and Fallen King, and Jake remains for the ritual. He makes visible visits to several factions and accepts Valhall's hospitality without joining. Meanwhile, the shapeshifting primordial cannot recognize the Malefic Viper's First Sage or that title.

Jake spars Carmen under restrictions, and their contest ends without a winner before they become partners. Carmen still intends to become Valdemar's Chosen and prefers that Jake not enter Valhall above her. Jake then takes control of the Fourth Hell prince's evolution ritual after estimating only an even chance of success. Ten crystallized hearts and Jake's origin energy form a superior Cerulean Devil heart, but its records manifest as a mindless husk inside the prince's soul space and begin consuming him. Jake enters that soul space, restrains the manifestation, and forces it to accept absolute submission to the prince. The prince survives and evolves into a full demon lord. The Malefic Viper explains that the success publicly demonstrates Jake's ability to apply his unusual origin power for other factions. The new demon lord owes Jake a major boon and gives him a crest whose bearer will be honored in the first four hells. With his Nevermore City obligations complete, Jake chooses to return home.

Jake returns to the Order after enormous gains in race, class, and profession levels. The Malefic Viper warns him not to discuss the First Sage except in narrowly defined circumstances. At his residence, Jake finds that Mira has become a High Elf, received Duskleaf's True Blessing, freed her former clan from slavery, and grown into an independent political figure. Erin visits to consider the Fourth Hell crest. In the Pantheon of Life, Yggdrasil examines Dina and finds that prolonged proximity to Jake has changed her soul without mutating it. Artemis has also been affected after far less exposure and now wants a future personal relationship with Jake as well as the chance to teach him archery. Yggdrasil permits the possibility but urges restraint. Sandy returns to Jake and explains that restrictions may prevent direct action against Earth's coming Prima Guardian, although indirect help remains possible. Satisfied that Mira no longer depends on him, Jake leaves the Order with Sandy and heads back to Earth.

Jake and Sandy arrive in Haven. The original forest settlement remains recognizable, but the former Fort has become a metropolis with major racial, cultural, and security tensions. Jake receives a detailed report and decides to leave political intervention to Miranda unless she requests his help. Sandy visits Arnold's workshop and becomes the subject of research into subspace travel, while Jake has Rick tend his time-affinity plant before continuing toward Skiggan. Near the city, vampires from the Sword Saint's clan attack the North Peak Wyvern. The wyvern defeats them and freezes the survivors in its cave. Jake confronts it, learns that it attacks perceived inferiors and uses captives to feed an unusual mountain resource, and orders it to release the vampires and stop indiscriminate attacks. After consulting the Everfrost Dragon God, the wyvern submits to Jake and accepts his restrictions. In the Fourth Hell, the transformed demon lord credits Jake with his survival, and the ruling devil prepares closer relations with the Order and plans to elevate his son.

Jake reaches Skiggan and reunites with his parents, Caleb, Maya, and his nephew Adam. His parents report outside interest in his life, while Caleb admits that decades in Nevermore left him struggling to readjust to ordinary fatherhood. The Sword Saint, now patriarch of the Nobaru clan and a World Council member, learns that vampire clansmen remain missing after the wyvern raid and goes to investigate. He finds that Jake has already secured their release and accepts the resolution. Jake spends more than two quiet weeks with his family and receives a communication token that will allow future video calls. Sandy returns after helping Arnold study subspace travel and combine that knowledge with information from two spacecraft. Haven's integration strains remain for Miranda to address, the Prima Guardian event is still approaching, and several larger mysteries and political obligations remain open. With his family connection restored, Jake leaves Skiggan aboard Sandy and heads for the moon.

characters.description: Earth's world leader and the Malefic Viper's Chosen. He travels with Sandy to the Moon and detects an unidentified B-grade presence there.
characters.name: Jake Thayne

characters.description: Jake's cosmic-worm companion, able to carry passengers through subspace and navigate by sensing changes in space. Sandy transports Jake safely through the hostile layers around Earth and onward to the Moon for their investigation.
characters.name: Sandy

characters.description: Jake's primordial patron and remote adviser. He identifies the Lunewood meteorite as a system-planted object and believes the Moon's hidden B-grade is probably unable to leave, giving Jake strategic guidance during the lunar expedition.
characters.name: Malefic Viper

characters.description: A hostile B-grade plant-undead entity fused around the Moon's core. It attacks Sandy below the surface and reaches Jake through the Lunewood Forest with powerful but incoherent communication.
characters.name: Ghost Vine Sovereign

characters.description: A god who publicly confronts the Star-Seizing Titan and wounds the primordial with the Hero's Sword. The display strengthens his legend and increases the strategic threat surrounding Jake and the Malefic Viper.
characters.name: Yip of Yore

characters.description: Jake's wind-aligned companion. She volunteers to help the Sky Whale survey dangerous beasts and either bring them into Earth's defense effort or neutralize them before the Prima Guardian arrives.
characters.name: Sylphie

characters.description: A level-333 beast coordinating Earth's response to its most dangerous creatures before the Prima Guardian event. Sylphie volunteers to help recruit manageable beasts and neutralize those that remain a threat.
characters.name: Sky Whale

characters.description: An inventor, analyst, and space-travel researcher who studies the lunar threat with Jake. He takes Jake's old Katar apart to use its records in a stronger replacement weapon and continues developing technology for travel beyond Earth.
characters.name: Arnold

characters.description: Jake's stand-in world leader and Earth's practical political commander. Returning from Nevermore with a mobile witch domain, she resumes planetary administration and begins organizing leaders and defenses for the coming event.
characters.name: Miranda

characters.description: Miranda's assistant, newly returned from Nevermore as a capable C-grade Lucenti Mage. She supports the renewed effort to coordinate Earth's leadership and serves beside Miranda as preparations for the planetary event accelerate.
characters.name: Lillian

characters.description: A labyrinth-maker who proposes merging the available reward idols into one permanent training complex spanning E-grade through B-grade. Projections and repair clones will oversee the ambitious construction and its later maintenance.
characters.name: Minaga

characters.description: The primordial who facilitates the renewal of Jake and Sylphie's damaged Union Oath. Stormild restores their friendship bond, explains its anti-betrayal condition, and confirms that Sylphie has claimed an authority.
characters.name: Stormild

characters.description: A Vespernat Hive Queen who arrives on Earth with Sandy shortly before the Prima Guardian event.
characters.name: Vesperia

characters.description: Yip of Yore's Chosen and leader of the vast Prima Guardian Alliance. He coordinates hundreds of planets even though his own world appears strong enough to face its crisis without them, making the coalition's larger political purpose uncertain.
characters.name: Ell'Hakan

characters.description: A Risen envoy, curse specialist, and ally of Earth. He returns as the official representative of tens of thousands of Risen seeking a place in the coming campaign, giving his arrival both military and diplomatic importance.
characters.name: Casper

characters.description: A Holy Church augur returning to Earth with a Church contingent before the Prima Guardian event.
characters.name: Jacob

characters.description: A returning power whose destabilized realm is rebuilding as Earth prepares for the Prima Guardian.
characters.name: Fallen King

characters.description: A master swordsman whose clan controls the territory chosen for Labyrinth City and will manage the new settlement.
characters.name: Sword Saint

characters.description: A heretic metal and karma mage who returns early from Nevermore with urgent intelligence about Ell'Hakan. Jake and Miranda regard his information as important while remaining wary of his motives, methods, and stability.
characters.name: William

characters.description: A close-combat member of Earth's elite Guardian strike team. Her assigned task is to draw the enemy's attention while the other specialists establish their attacks, placing her at the center of the planned opening engagement.
characters.name: Carmen

characters.description: Jacob's distant guardian. He joins Jacob in confirming the predicted target area shortly before Earth's Prima Guardian arrives.
characters.name: Bertram

characters.description: A returning ally who arrives on Earth with members of a Tao sect before the Prima Guardian event.
characters.name: Aaron

characters.description: A Court of Shadows judge who joins Earth's elite Guardian strike team as a fast attacker.
characters.name: Caleb

characters.description: An investigator who leads inquiries into Earth-based collaborators because many suspects come from his former United Cities Alliance support base.
characters.name: Arthur

characters.description: A ranged combatant assigned to Earth's elite strike team for the immediate attack on the Prima Guardian. She joins the specialists gathered at the predicted impact site while the larger force prepares to contain the surrounding armies.
characters.name: Maria

characters.description: A level-349 composite enemy created under Earth's accelerated Guardian protocol. Its body combines traits and energies drawn from several Primas defeated earlier on the planet.
characters.name: Exalted Prima Guardian

characters.description: An injured world leader and spear fighter fleeing her planet's Honored Prima Guardian. A premature release has killed most of her elite force, and the enemy continues pursuing her through repeated attempts to escape.
characters.name: Oleandra

characters.description: An offworld leader who meets Oleandra after killing her planet's Prima Guardian and identifies himself only as Earth's world leader.
characters.name: Thane

characters.description: Jake's identity becomes known to Oleandra after their meeting, connecting him to the offworld leader who killed her planet's Prima Guardian.
characters.name: Jake Thayne

characters.description: The elven world's nominal leader and religious intermediary for the Great Bright One. He holds final authority over releasing the planet's Prima Guardian.
characters.name: Voice of the One

characters.description: The elf known as the Voice of the One and the effective leader of a vast unified population. He agrees to release his world's Prima Guardian after judging Jake capable of defeating it.
characters.name: Kindroth

characters.description: An overseer of Earth's returning Risen population. She works with Casper to keep the contingent disciplined as it settles on a self-governed island amid protests and anti-Risen incidents.
characters.name: Priscilla

characters.description: The swordsman known as the Sword Saint. He prepares a painting-based emergency return method before using Arnold's teleporter to travel to another world.
characters.name: Miyamoto

characters.description: A level-306 living calamity that drains color and life from its surroundings. It traps Sylphie and the Fallen King, survives devastating physical wounds, and spreads stronger desolation when injured, turning a direct battle into an escalating environmental disaster.
characters.name: Desolate Child of Loss

recaps.ending: Jake remains on Earth in a guarded recovery after the Malefic Viper repairs his shattered soul. His resource capacity is still reduced, and the corrupted half-core continues its extremely slow absorption inside a permanently sealed skill. Sylphie is alive after cleansing and evacuation, but has lost her right wing. The Fallen King apparently destroys himself and the Desolate Child of Loss in a soul explosion. His records and true soul survive inside the Mask of the Fallen King, although Aaron can find no means of revival. No kill notice confirms the Desolate Child's death, but new planetary desolation has stopped. William finds abnormal connections around the trap without proof that Ell'Hakan directed it. Miranda monitors Ell'Hakan-linked sleepers on Earth while covertly pursuing a separate fanatic network hostile to Jake, outsiders, and beasts. Ell'Hakan's alliance and Earth's coalition continue competing across the unfinished Prima Guardian event. Kindroth remains a useful but independent diplomatic ally, the Risen have a self-governed island settlement, and three beastfolk diplomats have reached Earth. The lunar Ghost Vine Sovereign and Operation Moonfall also remain unresolved.
recaps.in_short: Jake Thayne and Sandy discover a B-grade plant-undead fused with the Moon's core, but postpone Operation Moonfall to face the Prima Guardian event. Jake makes Earth's Guardian stronger by choosing an accelerated protocol, then kills it in space and claims Earth's pylon. Earth launches a rival rescue network as Ell'Hakan expands his own alliance. After blackened planets reveal a desolation threat, Jake takes half of a corrupted core into an absorption skill. The experiment nearly destroys his soul, and the Malefic Viper saves him by sealing the skill with the half-core inside. While Jake recovers, Sylphie and the Fallen King are trapped with the Desolate Child of Loss. Sylphie escapes after losing a wing, but the Fallen King stays behind and apparently disperses both himself and the enemy. His true soul remains in his mask. The book ends with Jake recovering, planetary desolation apparently halted, and Earth investigating sleeper agents and independent fanatics tied to Ell'Hakan's influence.

recaps.text: Previously: Jake Thayne is Earth's world leader and the Chosen of the Malefic Viper, though Miranda handles much of the planet's practical administration. Sandy serves as Jake's companion and transport, while Sylphie is his wind-aligned friend and fellow fighter. The Fallen King remains linked to Jake through soul magic, and the Sword Saint stands among Earth's strongest independent combatants. Arnold supports Earth through invention and analysis, while Casper connects Jake's circle to the Risen. Major figures are returning from Nevermore as the planet prepares for the Prima Guardian, a system event that will place Earth and its pylon at risk. Several powerful factions must cooperate despite their conflicting loyalties. Beyond Earth, the god Yip of Yore and his Chosen, Ell'Hakan, remain strategic rivals to Jake and the Malefic Viper. Their competition gives the coming planetary crisis a wider political dimension.

Jake and Sandy travel through subspace to investigate the Moon. Its far side contains the corrupted Lunewood Forest, an artificial ecosystem grown from a system-placed wood meteorite. Sandy descends toward the lunar core while Jake reaches the meteorite, which is dying and tries to take him as a host. Below the surface, Sandy encounters the Ghost Vine Sovereign, a B-grade plant-undead entity fused with the Moon's core. It attacks both explorers, and Sandy's mark disappears, making Jake believe his companion has died. Sandy instead triggers a prepared resurrection and returns through an egg-anchor. The revival saves two stomachs but destroys the others, including Jake's mobile alchemy laboratory, and leaves Sandy severely weakened. The Ghost Vine Sovereign appears largely instinctive and remains bound to the lunar core. Jake and Sandy agree that it must eventually be destroyed even if the Moon cannot be preserved, naming their future plan Operation Moonfall.

Sandy recovers enough to return Jake to Earth before leaving for further treatment. Jake resumes alchemy while Arnold begins rebuilding his Katar and studies the lunar danger. Sylphie helps the Sky Whale bring Earth's strongest beasts under control. Miranda and Lillian return from Nevermore and organize planetary leadership, while Minaga begins combining several rewards into a permanent labyrinth spanning multiple grades. Stormild renews Jake and Sylphie's Union Oath and leaves Jake an unexplained request concerning a mutual acquaintance. Preparations intensify for the Prima Guardian, whose victory would cost Earth its planetary pylon. Ell'Hakan, Yip of Yore's Chosen, leads an alliance of nearly five hundred planets even though his own world can likely survive without it. Casper returns as an envoy for a large Risen population, Jacob seeks entry with a Holy Church group, and Sandy arrives with Vesperia, a Vespernat Hive Queen.

Vesperia reveals herself as a true royal of the Endless Empire with an internal hive, a large drone army, subordinate queens, and elite Queen's Guards. Her authority lets her bring Earth's underground hives into the defense plan without open war. At the World Congress, Jake imposes Earth's rules on hostile visiting factions while Miranda assigns forces for the coming event. Jacob's vision locates the likely desert impact site, and Arnold supplies communications, a legendary void-based Katar, and adaptive armor. William returns early from Nevermore with evidence that Ell'Hakan's homeworld is held by bloodline-reinforced devotion. He believes Ell'Hakan plans to gain influence over world leaders and pylons, but the unknown sponsor behind William's investigation remains unexplained. Earth decides to compete for other worlds after securing itself. Jake leads a compact team of close combatants, ranged attackers, a healer, and other specialists to the confirmed arrival zone while the wider army establishes a perimeter.

Jake enters the arriving vessel alone and accepts an accelerated protocol that immediately frees an enhanced level-349 Exalted Prima Guardian. The strike team attacks as the creature adapts its body to different damage types. Vesperia loses all four Queen's Guards protecting her and restraining the enemy. Arnold contributes an orbital strike, an android decoy, and remote void fire. Maria and Casper are forced out, Aaron is separated, and the Sword Saint, Vesperia, the Fallen King, Carmen, and Caleb suffer severe injuries. William disrupts the orders holding Aaron away, allowing the healer to restore the team. Near defeat, the Guardian copies the Malefic Viper's escape function and flees into space. Jake follows alone, upgrades his wings under the strain, and fights it above Earth. He tears apart most of its remaining body with a concealed arcane attack. The final fragment tries to copy Jake's time-altering ability, fails, ages into ash, and dies. Earth has defeated its Guardian, but Jake is blind, depleted, and waiting in space for Sandy.

The Guardian's death weakens the remaining Primas, allowing Miranda to coordinate Earth's cleanup. Sandy retrieves Jake while he chooses Lone Hunter of Horizon's Edge, committing his class toward solo hunts rather than a permanent party. Once Earth is secure, Jake opens the captured vessel and learns that he ranks first among candidates for the Seat of the Exalted Prima, ahead of Ell'Hakan and an unidentified survivor. Jake claims Earth's planetary pylon, placing its civilization pylons under his authority and granting benefits to the planet's population. The strike-team contributors receive legendary rewards, while Jake receives the still-sealed Seal of the Exalted Prima. The vessel also provides a route into the Alliance teleportation network. Earth begins a wider intervention campaign: Vesperia, Sylphie, and the Fallen King form one group, the Court of Shadows deploys under Caleb, and the Sword Saint and Jake choose separate targets. Miranda, Arnold, and William remain involved in developing broader travel beyond Alliance-controlled destinations.

Earth's hunters begin rescuing other worlds. Vesperia, Sylphie, and the Fallen King clear a weak dwarf-and-ant-hive world and leave its hive in political control. Jake reaches Oleandra's planet after a disastrous early Guardian release has killed most of her elite force. He saves the survivors, kills the Guardian, and warns Oleandra that Ell'Hakan's bloodline can distort emotions. Her world considers cautious contact with Earth. Jake then notices the first fallen planet on the vessel map. On a powerful elven world, he proves his strength while hiding much of it and confronts the leader known as the Voice of the One over exaggerated religious claims. The leader is Kindroth, who ultimately releases the Guardian. Jake kills it with one prepared attack, and Kindroth claims the pylon. Kindroth then becomes Jake's political sponsor, gathering world leaders willing to accept Guardian help without joining Ell'Hakan. Jake gains a list of new destinations, turning individual rescues into a voluntary coalition.

Jake's campaign expands rapidly, and Earth-associated forces clear more than a hundred Guardians. Kindroth organizes access while Miranda evaluates him as an effective but independently motivated ally. A new danger appears when cleared planets turn black on the map, meaning their cores have been destroyed beyond reclamation. During a divided scale-kin world's crisis, Jake avoids a staged confrontation with two leaders aligned to Ell'Hakan. He performs a deliberately misleading melee-only Guardian kill, prompting Yip of Yore to consider recruiting him as a possible usurper of the Malefic Viper or killing him if he refuses. Meanwhile, the Risen receive a self-ruled island on Earth. Arnold's experimental long-range circle lets Jake reach the first blackened world. He finds an airless ruin saturated with desolation and a corrupted planetary core spreading permanent damage. Evidence suggests a limping humanoid entity infused part of its own soul into the core. Jake discovers that his Malefic Viper abilities offer some protection and decides to take a fragment.

Jake tries to remove a small fragment from the corrupted planetary core but breaks it in half. He stores the smaller half inside his absorption skill and escapes to Earth as desolation floods the skill's internal stomach. Aaron keeps him alive while Jake builds a containment structure in his soul space. Jake then applies his primeval origin energy directly to the skill's symbolic representation, triggering an uncontrolled evolution that consumes his soul-space resources and destabilizes his soul. The crisis also injures the Fallen King through their connection. Jake prepares to destroy the skill rather than die, but the Malefic Viper intervenes despite the system's restrictions. He stops the evolution, repairs Jake's shattered soul, and freezes the damaged records. The intervention permanently seals the absorption skill's internal stomach, leaving the half-core trapped inside and only slowly being absorbed. Jake survives with sharply reduced resource capacity and begins a long natural recovery, now owing his patron an even greater debt.

Miranda conceals Jake's condition while Aaron limits his exertion, alchemy, boosting skills, and soul strain. Vesperia returns to protect him, and Sylphie stays until he can defend himself before resuming the wider campaign. The Sword Saint interrupts a civil conflict on a beastfolk world, forces its three kings into negotiations, kills its Guardian, and returns with three diplomats while the political outcome remains unresolved. Ell'Hakan asks Jacob to steer Jake away from the Malefic Viper, while Jacob warns that the conflict between the two Chosen is moving toward one of their deaths. Earth and Ell'Hakan's Holy Church-backed alliance continue competing across the galaxy as desolation consumes more worlds. Sylphie and the Fallen King clear about thirty planets together. On their latest world, its leader kills herself after activating the vessel, trapping them outside its teleportation room. William and Miranda uncover Earth infiltrators linked to that planet and learn their objective is to impose a fate worse than death on Jake. As Sylphie reports the trap, the horizon around her and the Fallen King begins losing color to approaching desolation.

Sylphie and the Fallen King face the Desolate Child of Loss, a living calamity that regenerates massive physical damage and spreads stronger desolation when harmed. Sylphie loses her right wing and amputates it before the contamination can spread. Jake ignores the risk to his damaged soul and travels with Sandy, Aaron, and William to extract them. Aaron cleanses Sylphie, but the Fallen King's desolation is too deeply embedded for Sandy to absorb him in time. He remains behind, transfers his mask into Jake's possession, and burns his soul to hold off the Child while the others escape. The Fallen King attacks the creature's soul and ends in a golden explosion that disperses them both. Jake wakes on Earth after nearly three days. The mask contains the Fallen King's records and true soul, but Aaron finds no reviving spark or restoration method. No kill notice confirms the Desolate Child's death. William can no longer locate its karma and finds abnormal connections to Jake and Ell'Hakan, but no proof that Ell'Hakan knew of or directed the trap.

Earth's investigation separates two hostile networks. Miranda monitors sleeper agents who report to Ell'Hakan but have not yet acted openly. A second, independent fanatic movement targets Jake and the Malefic Viper while recruiting anti-immigrant and anti-beast natives. William cannot reliably identify every member or trace the exact role of bloodline influence, and he refuses direct contact with Ell'Hakan because of the danger to his own stability. Miranda covertly hunts selected threats through her connection to Haven. Elsewhere, Jacob observes that no new planets are becoming desolate and privately infers that Jake's side probably stopped the calamity, though he withholds that conclusion from Ell'Hakan. The Desolate Child's death remains unconfirmed, and the organizer of the trap is still unknown. Jake keeps the Fallen King's true soul safe in the mask and continues his guarded recovery while Earth's coalition and Ell'Hakan's alliance press on with the unfinished Prima Guardian campaign.

characters.description: Earth's leading hunter and the Malefic Viper's Chosen is recovering from a serious wound to his soul. With the desolation threat unresolved, he favors taking the initiative against Ell'Hakan instead of waiting for another attack.
characters.name: Jake Thayne

characters.description: A Valhal-linked fighter and adviser who shares Jake's concern about Ell'Hakan. Her experience with false gods leads her to warn that destroying their visible form may not end them while their bond to faith remains.
characters.name: Carmen

characters.description: Yip of Yore's Chosen and the leader of an expanding coalition connected to the Holy Church. Jake regards him as Earth's principal political rival and suspects, without proof, that he is linked to the recent desolation.
characters.name: Ell'Hakan

characters.description: Earth's chief political organizer as the Prima Guardian event approaches its end. She gathers leaders and allies around a policy that offers influence and mutual protection to other worlds without direct conquest.
characters.name: Miranda

characters.description: A political participant who reports on the remaining Prima Guardian worlds and their competition for outside assistance.
characters.name: Kindroth

characters.description: A senior ally and battlefield commander who supports acting against Ell'Hakan but stresses that victory is not enough. Any operation must prevent the target from escaping and ensure that the threat is ended.
characters.name: Sword Saint

characters.description: A karmic mage working with Earth's leadership as both an intelligence asset and operative. He helps identify a covert observer serving Ell'Hakan and the Holy Church during the political meeting at Jake's lodge.
characters.name: William

characters.description: An inventor and technical adviser who proposes isolating Ell'Hakan inside a void sphere to block escape and outside aid. He understands the design but cannot yet supply a version adequate for the planned confrontation.
characters.name: Arnold

characters.description: An Endless Empire true royal who participates in Earth's strategic council. She favors a severe preemptive response to Ell'Hakan's most devoted supporters.
characters.name: Vesperia

characters.description: One of the five leading candidates promoted as administrators when the Milky Way completes the Prima Guardian event.
characters.name: Kindroth

characters.description: A rival primordial who turns the Malefic Viper's apparent injury into an opportunity. He launches a broad offensive against the Order and uses the Viper's silence to strengthen his own account of the conflict.
characters.name: Yip of Yore

characters.description: Jake's primordial patron and the leader of his Order. After confirming that the lingering desolation is probably a false god, he proposes turning Ell'Hakan's hopes for Jake's betrayal into the basis of a larger deception.
characters.name: Malefic Viper

characters.description: A karmically perceptive observer who detected the Malefic Viper's intervention in the restricted universe. His conclusion helped Yip of Yore verify that the primordial had acted and paid a significant price.
characters.name: Eversmile

characters.description: Valhal's first Valkyrie and a central political authority. She directs Carmen to bring Jake into Valhal territory while keeping the coming confrontation between the two primordials insulated from outside interference.
characters.name: Gudrun

characters.description: A powerful Valhal figure bound to help create the conditions for Yip of Yore and the Malefic Viper to settle their conflict. His assigned role is to prevent outside forces from intervening or deciding the confrontation.
characters.name: Valdemar

characters.description: An unidentified man who resists the desolation on a ruined world, retrieves its surviving heart-like fragment, retracts the spreading corruption, and seals the fragment in a box. His identity and purpose remain unknown.
characters.name: Unnamed Man with Desolation Fragment

characters.description: Jake's wind-aligned companion, chosen to travel with him and Carmen into Valhal territory. Her presence among the small party helps demonstrate that Jake is willing to trust Valhal during the developing negotiations.
characters.name: Sylphie

characters.description: The leader of a heavily protected Valhal world and Jake's local host. He receives Jake's party, helps shape their political approach, and presents Valhal as a possible future home and source of protection for the hunter.
characters.name: Bobby

characters.description: A Holy Church augur who serves as the Church's representative when the protected negotiations with Ell'Hakan begin.
characters.name: Jacob

characters.description: The Boundless Hydra leading the Order's defense while the Malefic Viper remains isolated. He directs the surviving allied gods to withdraw toward Primordial 4, protect Order members, and avoid unnecessary battles.
characters.name: Lord Protector

characters.description: A labyrinth-maker who observes the sealed divine duel alongside the Worm God. He is already occupied with designing the labyrinth intended for the next era, giving him a direct interest in how the struggle between primordials concludes.
characters.name: Minaga

characters.description: A spatial creature able to carry large strike forces across galactic distances. Sandy can reach places already visited or detected, but distance, energy demands, preparation time, and destination knowledge constrain the jumps.
characters.name: Sandy

characters.description: Jacob's guardian, left behind after the augur escapes with the remnants of Ell'Hakan's soul. He remains to face an exhausted Jake on the collapsing planet.
characters.name: Bertram

characters.description: Ell'Hakan's former right-hand leader and the figurehead of the remaining committed loyalists after Ell'Hakan's death. The leader's identity and ultimate fate remain unresolved.
characters.name: Former Loyalist Leader

characters.description: A pre-System librarian encountered inside a mutable record-world. Known as the Malefic Viper's legendary teacher, he asks Jake to preserve memories of a forgotten city that survives only through his recollection.
characters.name: First Sage

characters.description: A Crimson Flame fire archer and skilled bowyer being urgently recalled from an attempt to earn a high-level dungeon's first-clear title. Jake hopes she can help replace his failing bow.
characters.name: Maria

recaps.ending: Jake ends Ell'Hakan's Celestial Child transformation and returns to Earth, allowing Miranda to turn his victory into momentum for a new galactic order. The remaining loyalists are losing ground, but their leadership is still active and the Holy Church retains influence across former coalition worlds. Jacob carries Ell'Hakan's true soul under a Church contract. Although Jacob and Bertram oppose restoring Ell'Hakan in any meaningful sense, a Church faction plans a brief resurrection to preserve his coercive bloodline. Jake considers recovery of the soul nonnegotiable and prepares to approach the Church with Carmen held in reserve. The Malefic Viper has killed Yip of Yore and is slowly absorbing the selected records he made into an alchemical treasure. Jake is promised a supervised share later. The First Sage's lesson has strengthened Jake's soul and left him a legacy book with possible healing guidance, but his old soul wound still prevents a safe evolution to B-grade. Jake finishes a temporary arcane bow using Maria's Titanwood weapon and owes her a bounded favor. The desolation threat, Minaga's unfinished Earth labyrinth, and Earth's political consolidation remain unresolved.
recaps.in_short: As the Prima Guardian event ends, Jake and the Malefic Viper stage a public rupture to strengthen Yip of Yore's confidence and secure a temporary galactic truce. Yip attacks the Order but discovers that his apparent victory was a trap: the Viper uses a dragon molt and Malefic Alchemy to kill him and harvest selected records. Ell'Hakan inherits willing remnants of Yip's legacy, prompting Jake to attack his homeworld. Their duel escalates when Ell'Hakan's bloodline turns his Celestial Child claim into absolute self-delusion and his followers sacrifice themselves to sustain him. Jake destroys the transformed soul and stops its final Eclipse. Jacob nevertheless removes Ell'Hakan's true soul for a Holy Church faction seeking to preserve the bloodline. While Earth advances against the remaining loyalists, Jake enters an interactive record of the First Sage, gains control over his soul space, and receives a legacy book that may heal his lingering injury. He then reforges Maria's Titanwood bow and prepares, with Carmen as backup, to reclaim Ell'Hakan's soul from the Church.

recaps.text: Previously: Jake Thayne returned from Nevermore carrying a serious injury to his soul and remained the Malefic Viper's Chosen. Earth emerged as a leading power in the Milky Way, but its contest with Ell'Hakan and his Holy Church-linked coalition remained unsettled. The galaxy was still completing the Prima Guardian event, whose end would reopen political competition among its worlds. The Fallen King's apparent sacrifice stopped a desolation entity, yet the creature's true end was uncertain and its loss remained personal for Jake. As the new volume begins, Jake is close to recovering physically, the wider galaxy is nearing a major realignment, and Ell'Hakan remains the opponent most likely to exploit it.

The final Prima Guardian falls after a suspicious delay on a world controlled by Ell'Hakan's side. Before that happens, Jake and Earth's leaders prepare for the political opening that will follow. They favor alliances and influence over direct conquest, while quietly considering an offensive against Ell'Hakan. Arnold proposes a void sphere to prevent escape, and Jake completes a one-use arrow built around Eternal Hunger. The system names the Milky Way the first galaxy to finish the event and promotes Jake, Ell'Hakan, and three others as leading administrator candidates. The transition immediately becomes a crisis. Ell'Hakan-linked gods, the Holy Church, and monster forces exploit teleportation networks, foment unrest, and compete for authority on vulnerable worlds. At the same time, Yip of Yore attacks the Order of the Malefic Viper after the Viper's costly intervention in the restricted universe becomes known. With Earth facing coordinated disruption and the Order retreating, Jake seeks direct contact with his patron.

The Malefic Viper confirms that the desolation entity was probably a false god and may survive while sustaining faith remains. He then gives Jake a strategy for the larger conflict: Jake will appear to rebel against him, claim that the Viper trapped and poisoned his Chosen, and seek Valhal's protection as a prospective usurper. The apparent betrayal is intended to reinforce Yip of Yore's narrative and create room for a temporary truce with Ell'Hakan. Jake briefs a small Earth circle, while Miranda and the Sword Saint arrange for the rest of Earth's leadership to appear unconvinced by his defection. Carmen and Sylphie accompany Jake into Valhal territory. Valhal's leaders have their own obligations around the coming divine confrontation, and an unidentified figure separately seals a surviving heart-like desolation fragment. On a protected Valhal world, Bobby hosts Jake and helps frame a negotiated surrender as a political victory for Ell'Hakan. The chapter closes inside a shielded conference with Ell'Hakan, Jacob, and an allied representative, where Jake's failed attempt to renounce the Viper's blessing makes his story appear credible.

Jake builds his false account from genuine secrets, including the Malefic Viper's blood inside his soul and the fact that only one of their deaths could end the true blessing. Ell'Hakan and the Holy Church accept a temporary territorial truce, while Valhal publicly supports Jake as a possible future usurper. The agreement permits evacuations and returns, but it also lets some worlds leave Earth's alliance and strengthens doubts about Jake's loyalty. As the Order's war worsens, Valhal completes a divine ritual that could transfer the Viper's path to Jake if the primordial dies. Jake has no intention of using it, yet his participation makes the performance more convincing. He spends the waiting period learning Valhal's alchemy and creates new malefic body potions, gaining several levels. Meanwhile, the Order withdraws toward Primordial 4 as gods defect or die. Yip of Yore finally arrives there with more than a thousand gods. The Lord Protector shields the central city, Eversmile observes, and Valdemar enters to remove outside interference. Jake prepares to denounce his patron before the gathered multiverse.

Jake publicly renounces the Malefic Viper while Miranda seals Earth from outside communication. Yip of Yore then traps himself and the Viper inside a pinnacle-grade void sphere for a duel with only one survivor. Yip understands that Jake's break is partly theatrical, but accepts the benefit it gives his legend. The duel escalates from physical exchanges to high-level conceptual combat. Yip's Hero Sword and years of poison adaptation appear to neutralize the Viper's best-known advantages, and his transcendent ring lets him steal records from a defeated enemy. His apparent victory is the trap. The body he drains is a prepared dragon molt, which binds to him after he has exhausted his strongest abilities. The unharmed Malefic Viper reveals that he cultivated Yip's rise to obtain contemporary records of growth and momentum. He uses Malefic Alchemy to strip away the parts he cannot use, preserves a small share for Jake, and consumes the rest as a treasure that will take years to absorb. Yip dies. When the void sphere collapses, the Viper returns to Primordial 4 and kills the opposing gods through his released presence, publicly restoring the Order's supremacy.

Ell'Hakan had prepared for Yip's possible death. A Holy Church ritual transfers the willing remains of Yip's records and legacy skills to him, making him Yip's usurper. Across the Milky Way, Yip-aligned governments destabilize, the Holy Church fills the religious vacuum, and Miranda launches attacks on confirmed Ell'Hakan supporters. Sandy enables long-range deployments while Jake goes alone to Ell'Hakan's homeworld. He bombards the surface to force his rival into the open, then descends through the planet to its claimed pylon. A newly merged Divine Bargain skill lets Jake offer that pylon to the Malefic Viper, creating a threat Ell'Hakan cannot ignore. Although a Holy Church augur advises retreat, Ell'Hakan decides that flight would leave him permanently dependent on the Church. The rivals fight first in the core chamber, where the pylon and Ell'Hakan's sun-aligned domain give him an advantage. Jake forces the battle toward the surface and lands what appears to be a fatal ambush, but Ell'Hakan restores himself and invokes a powerful celestial sunrise. Jake also learns that Ell'Hakan can read involuntary emotional reactions, so even answering a question can surrender information.

Ell'Hakan's growing solar domain is sustained by the population's faith rather than his own reserves. Jake commits his full boosting abilities, survives a massive sunlight attack through Eternal Shadow, and strikes Ell'Hakan with the Eternal Hunger arrow. The wound should be decisive, but Ell'Hakan's dying bloodline turns his invented Celestial Child identity into absolute self-delusion. He remains the same person and soul, now empowered by genuine belief in the lie. Jake activates Arnold's incomplete Void Sphere to isolate them. Most of Ell'Hakan's followers then willingly sacrifice themselves, rebuilding his failing body with celestial energy and supporting new moon, star, and sun powers. Jake learns that every wound still deepens fractures in the transformed soul. The Divine Bargain eventually removes the planetary pylon, collapsing both the void sphere and the planet itself. Ell'Hakan begins an Eclipse powered by the remaining faith energy. Facing death, Jake upgrades Moment of the Primal Hunter and Timeless Focus, stops the world briefly, and places twenty-two arrows into the existing fractures. Their combined detonation destroys the Celestial Child state and disperses the Eclipse. Jake survives, badly injured, while the immediate planetary threat ends.

Ell'Hakan's final remnant recognizes the end of his delusion before fading. Jake receives confirmation that all of the rival's identities belonged to one person, along with a sealed Starlight Heart tied to the bloodline. The victory is incomplete: Jacob gathers the true soul for the Holy Church and escapes by exchanging places with Bertram. Bertram explains that a local Church faction wants only a short-lived resurrection capable of preserving the bloodline, while he and Jacob oppose that plan. Jake kills Bertram to maintain their cover, and Jacob later revives him. Back on Earth, Miranda uses Jake's visibly wounded return to confirm the victory and strengthen morale. Ell'Hakan's coalition divides among surrendering worlds, opportunistic neutrals, and committed loyalists. Earth begins a controlled galactic offensive while the Holy Church consolidates. The Malefic Viper confirms that Ell'Hakan's transformed soul was destroyed and leaves the C-grade dispute with the Church to Jake, promising only to prevent higher-grade interference. Miranda hides Jake's recovery while seeking the remaining loyalist leadership. Jake reaches profession level 300 and spends five charges to accept an unknown record experience related to the Malefic Viper, hoping it will lead him to the First Sage.

Jake enters a mutable record-world and meets the First Sage, a pre-System librarian and the Malefic Viper's teacher. The Sage asks him to preserve memories of a forgotten city and guides him through the history that led to the Viper's birth, training, and eventual rise. Jake witnesses the Sage's extraordinary early-System power and his chosen death at his reluctant disciple's hands. The Sage asks Jake to tell the Viper that he remains proud of him. He then unlocks more of Sagacity of the Malefic Viper, upgrading it to mythical, and places a record manifestation inside Jake's soul space for a final lesson. The manifestation repeatedly overwhelms Jake until he recognizes that the space is his own world and that its limits reflect his expectations. Jake rebuilds it as a living forest balanced among his three energies. His soul mutates into Anomalous Arcane Soul, gaining stability and more efficient resources at the cost of greater future advancement requirements. The Sage leaves a legacy book containing staged instruction and possible guidance for Jake's lingering injury. Jake returns to his laboratory less than a second after leaving, with the book still present in his soul.

Jake learns that the First Sage originated the foundational skills Meditate and Identify, knowledge that the Malefic Viper says must remain secret. He delivers the Sage's final message, and the Viper urges him to study the legacy book for a way to repair his damaged soul. Until the injury from Palette of the Malefic Viper is healed, Jake cannot safely evolve to B-grade. Earth and Valhal begin repairing relations after the staged alignment with Yip, while Miranda continues the galactic consolidation. Jake prepares to recover Ell'Hakan's true soul from the Holy Church. Carmen agrees to remain in reserve so his initial visit can appear to be a negotiation rather than an invasion, and Arnold also remains available if stronger support becomes necessary. Jake first needs a replacement bow. Maria returns from a dungeon attempt and offers several choices. Jake takes the ancient Mighty Titanwood Great Bow in exchange for a bounded medium favor, then sacrifices one of its functions and burns arcane pathways into it. The resulting Mighty Arcane Titanwood Great Bow is a usable but inferior temporary weapon. With it completed, Jake and Carmen are ready to approach the Holy Church, while Jacob still carries Ell'Hakan's soul.

characters.description: A highly capable lone hunter and poison alchemist travelling between Beast Lord dungeons. Jake relies on archery, close combat, heightened perception, and abilities connected to the Malefic Viper.
characters.name: Jake Thayne

characters.description: The Beast Lord of the Lucenti Plains and the target of Jake's second dungeon. It commands the local herd and remains at the central pond with three unusually powerful white does.
characters.name: Great White Stag

characters.description: A man shaped by memories of the harm he has caused, including killing his brother Hermann. He intends to turn the tutorial into the foundation of his power.
characters.name: William

characters.description: An Augur of Hope who teaches and encourages the surviving camp. He completes a leadership quest, spreads Holy Church teachings, and gains knowledge connected to the Holy Pantheon.
characters.name: Jacob

characters.description: A named member of the surviving camp who provides combat theory for the training that Jacob offers to people without combat experience.
characters.name: Bertram

characters.description: A Holy Church priestess who receives Jacob after his one-use revival outside the tutorial and Bertram after Jacob restores him. She is the daughter of the church Grandmaster overseeing their preparation and training.
characters.name: Inara

characters.description: The deity served by Jacob's Holy Church. She accepts the preserved souls of Jacob's followers under his existing agreement and stands behind the religious path now being prepared for him.
characters.name: Holy Mother

characters.description: A level-81 ratman that commands the reservoir mole-rat swarm through the Swarm Control Rod. Jake kills the controller and destroys the rod, eliminating the remaining swarm.
characters.name: Ratman Swarm Controller

characters.description: An armored, sword-wielding ratman that guards the final incubator in the Forgotten Sewers. It uses dark mana and a domain that suppresses the senses of Jake.
characters.name: Nest Watcher

characters.description: The divine patron and ally of Jake. He intervenes when another god attempts to claim the body of William, treats Jake as a friend, and provides information about Jacob, Bertram, and Casper.
characters.name: Malefic Viper

characters.description: After Jake kills William, this unidentified white-haired god removes the body. The Malefic Viper allows him to keep it only in exchange for a favor.
characters.name: White-haired god

characters.description: The god who claimed William's corpse now identifies himself as one of twelve primordials. He restores William to life and invites him to become a disciple.
characters.name: White-haired primordial

characters.description: The gold-tusked Beast Lord of the Valley of Tusks. It commands a horde of roughly one hundred Steel Tusk Boars.
characters.name: Horde Leader

characters.description: Jake and Caleb's father, remembered during Jake's dream of the family's last breakfast together before the system arrived. His present location and condition remain unknown.
characters.name: Robert

characters.description: Jake and Caleb's mother, remembered during the family's last visit before the system arrived. Jake had promised to return for her birthday, and her present fate remains unknown.
characters.name: Deborah

characters.description: Jake's younger brother. He lives near their parents and is married to Maya, who is expecting their first child when Jake last sees the family before entering the tutorial.
characters.name: Caleb

characters.description: Caleb's wife and Jake's sister-in-law. She is seven months pregnant with the couple's first child during Jake's last remembered family visit before the system's arrival.
characters.name: Maya

characters.description: The tree-like final ruler of the tutorial and master of the four Beast Lords. Vastly stronger than Jake, the King offers him a safe departure or a fight to the death.
characters.name: King of the Forest

characters.description: A fire-and-archery god who sponsored the tutorial and offers Jake post-tutorial training and a blessing. Jake receives the invitation alongside one from the Malefic Viper.
characters.name: Umbra

characters.description: A godly alchemist and disciple of the Malefic Viper who begins instructing Jake in alchemy within the Viper's time-dilated realm.
characters.name: Duskleaf

characters.description: A former coworker who returns to Earth among the undead. He carries a blessing respected and feared by the undead, but rejects leadership of their force.
characters.name: Casper

characters.description: The unnamed risen human who leads the undead forces returning to Earth. Casper refuses a leadership role, leaving her in command while his purpose remains separate.
characters.name: Risen-human leader

characters.description: A survivor who blames Jake for Joanna's death and attacks him after the return to Earth. Jake crushes his hand during the confrontation, then leaves him a healing potion.
characters.name: Mike

characters.description: A level-61 beast attempting to control the Pylon of Civilization in the forest. Jake kills it before claiming the pylon.
characters.name: Savage Mole Lord

characters.description: A powerful archer helping Jacob recruit and protect survivors outside a sealed city. She follows his group while appearing to pursue a separate purpose connected to a god.
characters.name: Maria

characters.description: A family friend travelling with Hank, Mark, and Louise through the transformed forest. Her social skills help her negotiate temporary refuge with the masked protector of a secluded valley.
characters.name: Miranda

characters.description: An axe fighter with a builder profession and the father of Mark and Louise. He loses an arm protecting his children from an Oakwood Tiger before Jake rescues the group and provides a potion that restores it.
characters.name: Hank

characters.description: Hank's nineteen-year-old son and the rescued group's healer. He survives the altered forest with his father, sister, and Miranda before the party receives shelter in Jake's valley.
characters.name: Mark

characters.description: Hank's twenty-two-year-old daughter and an evolved caster. She is one of four survivors rescued from an Oakwood Tiger and allowed to recover in Jake's valley.
characters.name: Louise

characters.description: An aggressive level-89 insectoid that appears to rule the underground biodome. It is a swift flier, but Jake defeats it after it fails to adjust its tactics.
characters.name: Alpha Mantis Scyther

characters.description: The unnamed D-grade fungal network that controls the underground biodome. It is the cavern's true ruler, and Jake cannot defeat it when it awakens.
characters.name: Biodome fungal network

characters.description: A level-90 wind-manipulating hawk that encounters Jake during his early flight practice. It corrects his wing movements and balance, accepts a stamina potion, and voluntarily returns to continue teaching him.
characters.name: Level-90 hawk

recaps.ending: Jake returns to an enlarged and dangerous Earth after killing the King of the Forest and receiving a claim to a Pylon of Civilization. He secures the King’s former territory, conceals the pylon in a waterfall valley, and remains the settlement's masked protector rather than its administrator. Miranda becomes his Viscount and city lord, while Hank, Mark, and Louise become citizens and construct a lodge over the hidden pylon. Jacob and Bertram lead a separate large survivor group under the Holy Mother's instruction to avoid both alliance and conflict with Jake, though Jacob and Jake exchange supplies and information. William has been revived by the white-haired primordial, and Casper returns as undead but chooses a separate path. Jake knows Robert, Deborah, Caleb, and Maya are alive, but he still does not know where to find them. His immediate challenges are developing a poison for the D-grade fungal ruler beneath the forest and mastering Wings of the Malefic Viper with help from a wind-manipulating hawk.
recaps.in_short: Jake clears the remaining Beast Lord dungeons, defeats William, and rejects the fate that expected him to die before the tutorial's end. Using revenge weapons left by the Beast Lords, poison, and the Great White Stag's unstable core shard, he kills the far stronger King of the Forest and finishes as the sole survivor recognized by the system. After training with the Malefic Viper and claiming dormant true blood without surrendering his independence, Jake returns to a transformed Earth. He reconciles partially with Jacob, learns his family is alive, claims a Pylon of Civilization, and hides it in a forest valley. Miranda takes charge of the new settlement while Hank, Mark, and Louise begin building it. Jake survives an encounter with the D-grade fungal ruler of an underground biodome, chooses wings at his next profession milestone, and ends the book learning to fly from a level-90 hawk.

recaps.text: Previously: Jake Thayne entered a deadly tutorial and developed into a formidable hunter and poison alchemist associated with the Malefic Viper. He became separated from former coworkers including Jacob, Bertram, and Casper as the tutorial's survivors divided into different paths.

Jake delays his next dungeon long enough to advance his alchemy and gain Scales of the Malefic Viper, then enters the Lucenti Plains. He studies its herd movements, clears the outer groups, and prepares an attack on the Great White Stag and its three white does. After killing the attendants, Jake discovers that the central pond and the outer ponds form a light-powered defensive network. He corrupts that network with poison and his own blood, causing a destructive collapse that injures both combatants. When the stag uses the remnants of its herd for one final attack, Moment of the Primal Hunter gives Jake the opening to evade it. He forces the exhausted level-93 stag into the poisoned pond and kills it, completing the dungeon. Elsewhere, Jacob advances as an Augur of Hope, preserves the willing souls of his followers, and appoints Bertram as a guardian whose life is bound to his own.

Jake recovers the unstable Corrupted Moon Core Shard from the Great White Stag and enters the Forgotten Sewers. Dense dark mana initially blinds him and disrupts his perception, but he adapts, learns to manipulate that affinity, and navigates the shifting maze. After destroying a controlled mole-rat swarm, he takes Descending Dark Fang and advances toward the nest. The armored Nest Watcher defends the final incubator with dark mana and a suppressive domain. Jake survives by closing into melee, breaking its leg, and allowing poison to finish the work. Before dying, the Nest Watcher asks him to kill the King of the Forest and leaves a one-use curse charged with its resentment. Jake clears the dungeon with new armor and three Beast Lords defeated. Meanwhile, William apparently kills Bertram and Jacob, but Jacob revives outside the tutorial through a one-use ability and restores Bertram. The pair enter Holy Church training under Inara's supervision.

William clears another dungeon and confronts Jake as the last visible rival. After William claims responsibility for the camp's deaths, Jake overwhelms and kills him. A white-haired primordial takes the body after the Malefic Viper secures a favor in exchange, and the Viper tells Jake that Jacob, Bertram, and Casper still exist. He also explains that the expected course of fate had Jake dying early, William becoming the primordial's disciple, and Jacob serving the Holy Mother. Jake's survival disrupted that forecast, and he commits to following his own choices despite a warning that he is not fated to defeat the forest king. The primordial revives William once and offers him discipleship. Jake scavenges equipment, enters the Valley of Tusks, and escapes its boar horde by inventing a dangerous stamina technique.
