During exhausted sleep, he remembers his parents Robert and Deborah, his brother Caleb, and Caleb's pregnant wife Maya. Their unknown fate becomes a central reason to return home.

Jake discovers that the boars drink from an earth-mana lake and develops a toxin that can spread through its magical source. The contaminated water blinds and disorients the horde, allowing him to kill most of it from concealment. He recovers, gains Limit Break, eliminates the remaining boars, and brings down the Horde Leader's defenses with a collapsing pillar and a fully charged Infused Powershot. In the final exchange, Jake closes to melee and poisons the wounded Beast Lord until its own last attack helps kill it. The level-99 Horde Leader leaves behind an Epic Tusk filled with hatred for the King of the Forest, matching the revenge purpose of the Nest Watcher's curse. With all four Beast Lords dead, Jake has completed the dungeon chain. The tutorial's final opponent is now forced to appear, while Jake holds two weapons specifically designed to weaken it.

The King of the Forest offers Jake an immediate safe conclusion to the tutorial or a lethal battle for a greater reward. Jake chooses to fight despite learning that his strongest shot barely scratches the D-grade, tree-like ruler. After being overwhelmed, he hides his plan behind ineffective attacks and slips the Nest Watcher's curse through the King's defenses. He then drives the Horde Leader's Tusk into its body. With the King's senses and energy impaired, Jake places the poisoned Corrupted Moon Core Shard into the wound and survives its explosion behind the Horde Leader's shield. Both fighters are left near death. The King uses soul magic to break Jake's consciousness, but an instinctive part of Jake takes control and pushes Limit Break beyond its safe threshold. Jake kills the level-136 King, overturning the forecast that he could not win. The system heals him, ends the tutorial, and moves him to a post-tutorial reward room.

The system credits Jake as the tutorial's sole survivor, grants exceptional titles and levels, and awards him control of one city-level Pylon of Civilization. From the tutorial store he chooses foundational tools and abilities, including two cauldrons, One Step Mile, an adaptable tool, and a perception-based gaze that merges with his enhanced sight. Jake accepts the Malefic Viper's invitation for accelerated training while Jacob and Bertram train separately with the Holy Church. In the Viper's realm, the godly alchemist Duskleaf helps instruct Jake. A poison trial secretly escalates when the Viper adds primordial blood, forcing Jake into a conflict within his own soul. Jake defeats a possible self defined by submission to the Viper and claims the true blood without abandoning his identity. His blessing and poison-related abilities grow substantially. He then chooses Sagacity of the Malefic Viper while rejecting devotional, sacrificial, and command-oriented paths.

Before Jake returns to Earth, the Malefic Viper confirms that Robert, Deborah, Caleb, and Maya are alive but withholds their location. The Holy Mother orders Jacob neither to oppose nor ally with Jake, while Casper returns among the undead and rejects their leadership. On the transformed and enlarged Earth, Jacob organizes survivors. He and Jake reach a limited reconciliation, exchanging potions and information before Jake departs. Casper silently acknowledges Jake but follows a separate route. Jake travels into the forest, kills the beast contesting a Pylon of Civilization, and claims it. The pylon makes him an Earl, but he refuses the city-lord profession to protect his alchemy path. He relocates the structure to a concealed waterfall valley and begins training and brewing there. Two weeks later, Jacob has gathered thousands of people with Bertram and the archer Maria, while Jake reaches the verge of another alchemy milestone in isolation.

Jake rescues Hank, Mark, Louise, and Miranda from an Oakwood Tiger, restores Hank's severed arm, and permits the four survivors to shelter in his valley. Miranda studies the masked protector and negotiates with him despite their differing views about leadership and violence. While exploring beneath the valley, Jake discovers an underground biodome. He kills its apparent mantis ruler, only to awaken the true D-grade fungal network controlling the plants, roots, fumes, and constructs throughout the cavern. Unable to make his existing poisons persist against it, Jake escapes and begins planning a toxin designed for plants or fungi. Returning to the valley, he offers Miranda operational control of the settlement. She accepts his Viscount title and the city-lord profession under a written agreement that leaves Jake with final veto and responsibility for protection. The hidden pylon now has a formal administrator, while Jake remains free to focus on strength and alchemy.

Miranda begins using her city-lord abilities to plan the settlement while keeping the waterfall valley and its pylon concealed. Hank becomes the main builder, Louise designs the structures, and Mark assists. Their first project is a lodge over the buried pylon with a secret cellar for Jake's alchemy laboratory. Jake studies how to create a slow poison capable of attacking the fungal network, then reaches level 70 in his alchemist profession. Given a choice between several Ancient abilities, he selects Wings of the Malefic Viper and starts learning to fly. His first attempts end in crashes, but continued practice lets him gain altitude and travel horizontally. Outside the settlement boundary, a level-90 hawk uses controlled wind and repeated physical corrections to teach him better balance and coordination. Jake rewards it with a stamina potion, and the hawk returns at night for another training session. The settlement is taking shape, the fungal ruler remains undefeated, and Jake's family is still alive but unfound.
